R3-1.headline: A bit better than even: the court leans to stablecoins taking almost nothing net from US deposits and money funds lately, and to most past growth being foreign, but nobody measures holders by country.
up: Issuer reports or the 2028-07-18 ban on non-permitted coins show a small US-held share of USDT
Supply grows again while US deposits and money funds keep rising
New IMF or Chainalysis flow studies again show North America as a net exporter of tokens
down: Regulator or issuer data put the US-held share above 50%
Supply passes $350B while US bank deposits fall
Stablecoins pass 10% of T-bills with mostly US buyers
R3-1.watch: Tether's Q3 attestation (about 2026-10-31), then total supply against $350B (new growth) or $250B (contraction)

R3-9.headline: About 7 in 10: likely that in a crisis Gulf and Asian states keep getting dollars mostly from their own reserves and Treasury sales, with the yuan as a trade top-up only.
up: The next Japan intervention again shows zero FIMA use while custody falls
Gulf states keep funding through record bond and sukuk issuance
Qatar-style PBoC swap renewals stay small next to Gulf dollar needs
down: H.4.1 shows FIMA above $1B or swap lines above $5B in a shock
An ESF statement reveals a Gulf or Asian swap line in use
A Gulf state signs a yuan-settled crude term contract
R3-9.watch: Weekly H.4.1 FIMA and custody lines, foreign official custody against $2.5T

R3-10.headline: About 2 in 3: if bills ever fall below 1.5%, issuers more likely cut payouts and fold into bank-type charters than win a gold door from Congress, and that test is unlikely before 2028.
up: The OCC approves floating-rate or short notes under clause (vii) without new law
More issuers take national trust charters after Circle
Circle cuts its 61.5% distributor payout as rates fall
down: A GENIUS amendment adds gold or longer notes as eligible reserves
Offshore issuers gain a large share and Congress widens reserves to compete
The OCC approves notes beyond 2 years
R3-10.watch: Fed path (December hike priced 75 to 79%), Circle's Q3 payout share, first clause (vii) requests after 2027-01-18

R3-2.headline: About 3 in 5: likely that housing caps how much of a printed UHI robots can meet, so a Musk-scale UHI runs about 6 to 10% inflation now rather than Round 2's 0.9%.
up: Shelter inflation stays above goods inflation in any period with large transfers
Productivity stays near 2% a year while capacity utilization stays below 79.4%
Housing completions stay near 1% of stock
down: Productivity above 4% a year with flat shelter inflation
Housing completions double with stable land prices
Humanoid shipments above 500,000 a year before 2029
R3-2.watch: Q3 productivity and labor share (early November 2026), then shelter vs core goods CPI

R3-8.headline: About 7 in 10: likely that the first US AI dividend is equity into locked accounts or a fund, not printed cash, and that no bill makes it pledgeable or programmable.
up: Treasury routes AI equity into Trump Accounts
The Sanders bill gains a number and cosponsors without a cash payout design
More states ban local guaranteed income
down: A bill with money finance or a CBO-scored cash UHI advances
Bill text allows assignment, payroll-deduction lending or token payment
A federal benefit is paid on a stablecoin rail
R3-8.watch: Any Treasury or White House AI equity announcement, and the first CBO score of an AI-dividend bill

R3-4.headline: About 2 in 3: likely that China extends the 10 November pause in some form, finalizes the solar know-how ban by mid-2027, and pairs it with only a thin yuan finance layer.
up: A numbered MOFCOM notice between 7 and 10 November extends Announcement 70
The final solar catalogue keeps the 70 µm and fluidized-bed bans
Yuan grows mainly through refinancing (Kenya-style) rather than new solar loans
down: Announcement 70 lapses with no replacement on 10 November
China drops the solar proposal after comments close on 15 November
Yuan-financed solar and battery projects abroad surge
R3-4.watch: MOFCOM announcement list from 7 to 10 November 2026, then comments closing 15 November

R3-12.headline: About 7 in 10: likely that electric freight swaps an oil flow dependence for a more concentrated but slower-acting battery stock dependence, centered on Chinese anode and LFP cathode.
up: IEA N-1 bars for anode and LFP cathode outside China stay below 100%
China's new-energy heavy truck share stays above 40%
No US LFP cathode plant reaches commercial scale by 2028
down: A China battery-material cut halts existing fleets within weeks
Non-China anode and LFP capacity exceeds demand outside China by 2030
US class 8 electric sales pass 2% with non-Chinese packs
R3-12.watch: EO 14421 rules on 24 December 2026, then IEA GEVO 2027 (May 2027)

R3-5.headline: About 2 in 3: likely that factory and robot building lowers home prices where land is cheap, while in coastal metros land absorbs most of the savings unless broad upzoning lets more homes share it.
up: Coastal cities delay broad upzoning (Los Angeles on SB 79)
Land shares keep rising in the FHFA update
Factory builders stay small (Reframe short of 114 units by about September 2027)
down: Factory-built homes sell near 20% below site-built in coastal metros
Montana or California by-right laws produce a permit surge with flat land prices
Coastal price to income falls without a demand drop
R3-5.watch: NAR first-time buyer profile (early November 2026) and SB 79 implementation fights

R3-6.headline: A bit better than even: likely that a human-made premium exists as a label effect in gifts, art and identity goods, but its cash size is unmeasured and platforms capture part of it.
up: The published Mandel and Imas paper reports sizable bid gaps
A marketplace discloses prices by provenance label with a premium
Provenance labeling rules spread
down: Replications find no label effect on what people pay
AI-made goods take share in gift and art categories at equal prices
Etsy's gross sales keep falling while its take rate rises
R3-6.watch: Etsy Q3 2026 (early November): take rate above 24% and gross sales trend

R3-11.headline: About 7 in 10: likely that child accounts as designed lift the bottom half's share of equities by tenths of a point at most, leaving it below 1% by 2045.
up: Seeds still need a family claim and top-ups stay flat rather than progressive
Employer contributions flow mainly to children of well-paid staff
The DFA bottom-half share stays between 0.53% and 0.66%
down: A statute routes $500B or more of AI equity to accounts
A national baby bond aimed at poorer children is enacted
Treasury data show contributions concentrated in low-income accounts
R3-11.watch: Fed DFA 2026 Q3 (about mid-December 2026), watching the 0.58% line

R3-13.headline: About 3 in 4: likely that deep prediction markets and the desk agree on direction on most shared events, with the desk's October hike line the one real miss.
up: The Fed holds on 28 October and hikes on 9 December
Stablecoins stay under $500B and CLARITY stays unsigned in 2026
Moody's affirms or cuts France roughly as the court expects
down: A deep market moves more than 15 points on Fed capture or Hormuz before year-end
The Fed hikes on 28 October
A federal Bitcoin purchase is announced
R3-13.watch: FOMC 28 October and 9 December, Moody's on France 23 October, then score the ledger on 31 December
